clue.text: Cereal, etc, going off with pressure inside container

indicators.note: inside says the pressure letter is placed within the jumbled letters
food going off has spoiled, so these letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: P is the standard physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Breakfast cereals and similar foods spoiling in a container under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' rearranges CEREALETC, and 'inside' puts P within that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any vessel or holder, a synonym for a container.

clue.text: Wandered around European city holding a daughter

indicators.note: a city holding something has it within its bounds, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
D is the usual abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone toured a European city, with a daughter along for the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandered around' is the whole definition, not a definition plus an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to travel aimlessly, the same as to wander about.

clue.text: Lower class?

parts.note: read as 'a class of things that low', i.e. moo, rather than people of low social rank

explanation.surface: A sociological label for the less privileged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' rhymes with 'mower' here: one who lows, as cows do, not the comparative of low.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and bulls moo, or low, so the herd is literally a class of lowing beasts.

clue.text: Those who join in leave regularly in chic underwear

parts.note: to part is to leave or depart

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words in chic, starting with the first

parts.note: pants are underpants

explanation.surface: People quitting at intervals while dressed in stylish underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' seems to go with 'leave', but it picks ICI from 'in chic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Participants are people taking part in an activity, i.e. those joining in.

clue.text: Long article about His Excellency

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
C is short for circa, Latin for about
HE abbreviates His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece of writing about an ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here, as in to yearn, not an adjective about the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn or pine for it.

clue.text: Almost furious with new husband-to-be? Relax here

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: livid means furious
a groom is a man about to marry

explanation.surface: A fiancé nearly losing his temper is told to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the D of LIVID. 'Relax' looks like an instruction to the angry groom but is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The lounge or sitting room is where a household unwinds.

clue.text: Theory Biden was ignoring all fringes

indicators.note: dropping the outer edge letters of each of the two words leaves only their centres

explanation.surface: A political remark about a US president who sidelined the extremes of his party.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a notion or concept, a near synonym in everyday speech.

clue.text: Editor upset over writer's report

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run upwards

parts.note: a scribe is a writer; the 's stands for 'is', joining to the definition

explanation.surface: An editor is unhappy with a journalist's piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ED to DE, and 'over' puts it above SCRIBE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To report an event is to give an account of it, to describe it.

clue.text: Followers advanced, shy about Liberal publication for teachers

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the shy word is wrapped around the next letter

parts.note: coy means shy
L stands for Liberal in party politics
the TES (Times Educational Supplement) is a British newspaper for teachers

explanation.surface: Bashful disciples reading a liberal teaching magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Acolytes are assistants or devoted followers, originally altar servers.

clue.text: Father's drunk a very English Brut, perhaps

indicators.note: someone drunk is jumbled and unsteady, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Dad has downed a very English dry champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges FATHERS into FTERSHA. Brut looks like the dry wine, but it is a brand of men's cologne.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut is a well-known brand of men's fragrance splashed on after a razor; 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: City in Czechoslovakia

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the long country name

explanation.surface: A question of which city lay in the former Czechoslovakia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside czechOSLOvakia; the city is not actually in that country.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, an example of a city.

clue.text: Consult a test, confused — we're looking for those with ability

definitions.text: we're looking for those with ability

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled, so the three words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Recruiters puzzled while checking a test to find gifted candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouts for talent seek promising people, e.g. young footballers or actors with skill.

clue.text: Den's after odd pieces of each cake

indicators.note: after places the den word behind the picked letters
the odd pieces are the first and third letters of each

parts.note: a lair is a den; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Den is grabbing bits of every cake, like a greedy soap character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Den' reads as a man's name (Den Watts of the British soap EastEnders) but means a lair; 'after' places it behind the picked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream, a type of cake.

clue.text: Uniform beginning to narrow somewhat below the belt

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: beginning to takes just the opening letter of narrow

parts.note: fairly means somewhat or rather

explanation.surface: A uniform that tapers a little beneath the waistband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below the belt' seems a place on the uniform but is an idiom for foul play.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing blow below the belt is illegal, so the idiom means in a way that is not fair.

clue.text: Variety show valued vile dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage show prized a lewd routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaudeville was American stage entertainment of mixed acts, a variety show.

clue.text: Brewed ideal beer — gas is foul

indicators.note: brewed implies ingredients mixed together, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: A homebrewer's perfect beer turns out to give off a nasty gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the anagram to the definition 'foul'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foul is unpleasant or nasty, a synonym.

clue.text: At home, answer female with whip without hesitation

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: At home, a woman answers the door holding a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly, instantly, as fast as a flash of light.

clue.text: Animal, pale brown, picked up noise finally — stand still!

parts.note: a stag is a male deer

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: tan is a pale brown colour

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of noise

explanation.surface: A light brown deer hears a sound and freezes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like hearing, but in this down clue it turns TAN into NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop moving or developing, as still water does.

clue.text: Mechanics might need to secure these basic details

definitions.text: Mechanics might need to secure these
definitions.meaning: threaded fasteners used by engineers to hold parts together
the practical fundamentals of a matter

explanation.surface: A garage workshop needing fasteners, then a manager wanting the fundamentals.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal fasteners and the idiom for practical fundamentals share one phrase.

clue.text: Rest strike an attitude again?

definitions.meaning: to rest is to lie or relax
to strike an attitude is to pose; doing so again is to pose a second time

explanation.surface: A model takes a break and then holds the pose once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading, RE (again) plus POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose means rest or calm; read as RE-POSE it means pose once more.

clue.text: Cunning wearing the man's suit

indicators.note: the man's is wearing the cunning, so it goes round it like clothing

parts.note: he's is a contraction of the man is
art means cunning or craft

explanation.surface: A sly fellow is dressed in someone else's suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a card suit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: I go on the run if I've gut wobbles

indicators.note: something that wobbles is unsteady, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous runaway confesses to bolting when his stomach turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway escaping capture is someone on the run.

clue.text: Same South American revolutionary replaces a plan

indicators.note: replaces says one letter of the first word is swapped out for the revolutionary

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: An unchanged rebel leader takes the place of a strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: CHE replaces the A in SAME, giving S-CHE-ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a plan or programme of action.

clue.text: Second best place to get off a bus?

definitions.text: place to get off a bus?

parts.note: top means best

explanation.surface: A passenger asking which stop is the next best one to alight at.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus stop is where passengers board and alight.

clue.text: A girl scratching rear, unfortunately

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, here the back letter of the girl word

parts.note: lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl awkwardly scratching her backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, akin to sadly.

clue.text: Nice meal of the day?

parts.note: Nice is the French Riviera city, so the dish of the day in French

explanation.surface: Asking about a pleasant daily menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, so the phrase is wanted in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for a restaurant's daily special dish.

clue.text: Turn, breaking off wide part of a shoe

indicators.note: breaking off means the wide letter is detached from the turning word

parts.note: to wheel is to turn
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: Twisting your ankle snaps off the broad part of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised back part under a shoe is its heel.

clue.text: Office workers surround drug dealers

parts.note: to pen is to enclose or surround
pushers sell illegal drugs

explanation.surface: Clerks hemming in narcotics traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-pushers are derided clerical staff doing paperwork.
